rv.q: Thus, I am happy report that this is a very funny "Nunsense," as directed by the veteran performer E. Faye Butler and choreographed by her pal, Kenny Ingram (once the baker opposite Donny Osmond in "Joseph"), here credited as Father Kenneth.
I suspect that today’s audiences will find this spiritually uplifting, Ecclesiastically-based musical comedy as much fun as audiences did over 40 years ago.
“Nunsense” delivers all of this and more and will be sure to keep you smiling from start to finish.
“Nunsense” is light entertainment that is sure to tickle one’s funny bone, supported by a cast that delivers a heavenly performance.
Nunsense is a fun idea, but the script fails to execute it satisfyingly.
The show directed by E. Faye Butler on a delicious set by Lauren Nichols is adorable and quite fast moving.
Ultimately, this production succeeds despite Nunsense rather than because of it.

cn.t: Critics find this nostalgic 1980s comedy a light, silly fundraiser romp with strong performances, though some question whether its dated humor and thin premise have aged well beyond its devoted fanbase.
